entities.text: Islavath Kamalamma vs The Special Deputy Collector
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus by declaring the action of the respondents in issuing proceedings in Rc.No.B1/746/06, dated 01.11.2008 declining to refer the matter to competent Civil Court for proper determination of the compensation amount with regard to acquisition of land in an extent of Ac.2.2 guntas situated in Sy.No.477/C and Ac.3.32 guntas situated in Sy.No.474 of Jallaram Village, Kamanpur Mandal, Karimnagar District as arbitrary, illegal, unjust, contrary to law, void abnitio, violative of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India, apart from being contrary to the various judgments of this Hon'ble Court and consequently direct the respondent to refer the matter to the Civil Court determination of proper compensation for the lands acquired in the extent of Ac.2.2 guntas situated in Sy.No.477/C and Ac.3.32 guntas situated in Sy.No.474 of Jallaram Village, Kamanpur Mandal, Karimnagar District under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act..."
2. Heard Learned Counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for the respondent.
SK,J 3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that this petition is filed by the petitioners challenging the impugned action of the respondent in issuing proceedings No.BI/746/06, dated 01.11.2008 declining to refer the matter to the Civil Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act,
1894.

The petitioner No.1 is the owner of the land to an extent of Ac.2.2 guntas situated in Sy.No.477/C and a further extent of Ac.3.32 guntas situated in Sy.No.474 of Jallaram Village,
Kamanpur Mandal, Karimnagar District were acquired by the respondent herein apart from other lands.

Due to the dispute between petitioners and others, the matter was referred to Senior Civil Judge, Peddapalli under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the same was numbered as O.P.No.322 of 1987 before the Senior Civil Judge, Peddapalli and the same was decreed on 20.07.2006 and declared the entitlement of the petitioners and others.
In view of the same, the SK,J petitioners herein filed copy application and the same was delivered on 10-10-2006.

Immediately,
after receiving the copy, the petitioners made application on 18.10.2006 to refer the matter to the Civil Court for proper adjudication with regard to determination of the compensation amount as the Islavath Kamalamma vs The Special Deputy Collector, on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170852307/
1 amount awarded was less than market value under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for enhancement of the compensation and the same was rejected by the respondent in impugned proceedings No.BI/746/06, dated 01.11.2008 on the ground that under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, six (6) months period is already been expired long back as on 14.12.1987.
4.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner further submits that the respondent ought to have seen that the period of two (2) months time prescribed for seeking to refer the matter to a Competent Civil Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act must be SK,J calculated from the date on which, the amount of compensation was received under protest or from the date of receipt of notice under 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act or from the date of receipt of the copy of the decree passed by the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The respondent has to refer the matter to the Competent Civil Court for proper determination of the compensation amount for the lands acquired by the respondents, otherwise, the petitioner and others would be put to grave and irreparable loss and hardship and requested to allow the writ petition.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners in support of his contention has relied upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Deputy Collector, Singareni Collieries Company Limited, Godavarikhani Vs. Dasari Ramulu and others 1. 2000 (2) ALD 418 (FB) SK,J 6.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, Singareni Collieries Company Limited, Godavarikhani Vs. Dasari Ramulu and others 1. 2000 (2) ALD 418 (FB) SK,J 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition basing on the counter averments submits that the award in the present land acquisition case was passed on 15.06.1987.
However the petitioner made an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act on 18.10.2006, which is after long gap of 19 years.
As per Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, an application for reference to the Civil Court shall be made within six (6) weeks from the date of the award.
Admittedly, the petitioners not made any application under Section 18 within six (6) weeks from the date of the award.

Therefore the respondent rightly issued the impugned memo dated 01.11.2008 rejecting the request of the petitioner in referring the matter to the Civil Court and there are no merits in the writ petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. After hearing both sides and perusing the record, this Court is of the considered view that the respondent- SK,J Land Acquisition Officer passed award on 15.06.1987 and referred the matter under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act to the petitioners and others and the same was disposed of by the Senior Civil Judge, Peddapalli in O.P.No.322 of 1987 dated 20.07.2006.
8.
Thereafter, the petitioners made copy application and obtained certified copy on 10.10.2006 which was decreed on 20.07.2006.

Admittedly, the respondent had not issued any notice under Section 12 (2) of Land Acquisition Act for communicating award to the petitioners herein and without ascertaining the share of the petitioners in the Award till the disposal of the reference under Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act and the Land Acquisition Award is not in force and the question of seeking enhancement does not arise and the Competent Civil Court passed Decree under reference on 20.07.2006.

Subsequently, the petitioners made copy application and obtained decree and filed within time i.e., SK,J within six (6) months as there is no notice issued by the respondent Islavath Kamalamma vs The Special Deputy Collector, on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170852307/
2 as under Section 12 (2) of Land Acquisition Act.

sentences.text: 9. In view of the same, the respondent cannot deny the case of the petitioners for reference of the matter Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act for determination of the enhancement of compensation.

10. The relevant portion of the Judgment relied by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners in Special Deputy Collector, Singareni Collieries Company Limited, Godavarikhani Vs. Dasari Ramulu and others (Supra-1) is as follows:
"32. Mere knowledge of the award cannot commence the period of limitation or set the period of limitation to run against the claimant depriving of his right to seek the reference.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, Singareni Collieries Company Limited, Godavarikhani Vs. Dasari Ramulu and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well known that the legal provisions of limitation are artificial and would not always satisfy the test of either logic or equality.
The provisions are being enacted with an object in a civilized society that the sword of Damocles should not SK,J be kept hanging for all times to come.
It does not obliterate the right but only bars the remedy.
As a necessary corollary the limitation cannot commence on the knowledge of an award when statute provides that it would commence from the date of service of the notice.
The commencement of the limitation has been provided by the Legislation by legal fiction, which should be taken to a logical end.
Neither the limitation can be extended nor we can read into the statutory provisions especially when they are not capable of two interpretations at all.

In our considered view since the period of limitation provided is six months from the date of award, interpreted to be the date of knowledge, the commencement of six months would not be attracted to the specific statutory provisions providing for the commencement of the limitation of two months from the date of service of the award.
The limitation cannot run against the claimant.
In spite of no form of notice or mode of service of the award having been provided yet service of notice has been specifically provided for.

Service of notice can safely be considered to mean tender of the notice to the claimant and not his mere knowledge acquired through various means".
11.
The above finding of the Full Bench of this Court is squarely apply to the instant case as the respondent not issued any notice to the petitioners under Section 12 (2) SK,J of Land Acquisition Act.

In view of the same, the petitioners filed application for reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 within time and the impugned orders passed by the respondent is liable to be set aside.

12. In view of the above findings, the writ petition is allowed by setting aside the impugned orders passed by the respondent in proceedings.No.BI/746/06, dated 01.11.2008 and directing the respondent to refer the matter as per Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 within eight (8)
weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
13. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
